title: Should you buy this instead of a slingshot? (Bench daddy review)
summary: Review of the Bench Daddy, a stiffer two-sleeve slingshot that deloads the bottom of horizontal presses. It let him bench heavy again and rehab a shoulder ruined by touch-and-go benching, but it has a learning curve, mostly builds triceps, and needs chest accessories added afterward.

claims.claim: The Bench Daddy is a thicker slingshot with two sleeve layers; the more sleeves you use, the more resistance it gives.
A slingshot adds energy at the bottom of the press, deloading the shoulders and chest; it takes roughly 30-40 lb or more off depending on the person.
It costs about $70, more than a Mark Bell slingshot.
Its wide, stretchy sleeves suit big-armed lifters; regular slingshots often stop fitting as you grow, while this one, bought for your bodyweight (his was about 210-220 lb), lasts for life.
The stitching is extremely durable and it doesn't really need washing or get smelly.
Use it mainly for bench press, but also push-ups and dips; with push-ups it allows tons of reps while sparing the shoulders and loading the triceps.
It does little for vertical presses like the overhead press because of the biomechanics; it is meant for horizontal presses.
A slingshot is valuable if a shoulder injury makes normal benching painful.
He ruined his right shoulder doing touch-and-go bench; the slingshot let him bench heavy again and served as rehab until he could bench without it.
The Bench Daddy has a learning curve: at first it is so stiff you can't touch your chest and it feels odd on the shoulders, unlike easy red/yellow slingshots.
Raw powerlifters should use one sleeve; shirted benchers can use the second to mimic a bench shirt without the hassle.
Because it deloads the bottom, it doesn't work the chest much; if your main bench sets use it, add a chest-targeting accessory afterward.
Slingshot benching blows up the triceps but does little for shoulder and pec hypertrophy.
It suits lifters with a shoulder injury, lagging triceps, or high bench volume who want to bench more often without pain.
The Bench Daddy is the only reason he can still bench heavy.
